author: Ngagescott
title: Primitive could be so much better
body:
First of all - reading the recent reviews are obviously employees, they marvel at the convenience of just picking up their phone to control their AC? Really, most people just call that an App…
The schedule function is too tedious, they should take some cues from Nest. Ecobee does the same nonsense, it doesn’t need to be difficult. The History shows only 2 modes 100% and less. So if the compressor is running at 95% then it gives the user the impression that they are saving energy, too course. Where is the cutting edge sophistication in that. Trane sells one of the most expensive systems, I wish they’d increase their software budget to better reflect the product line. Very disappointed with this app.

author: n1weather
title: Lacks functionality other apps/thermostats have had for a decade or more
body:
This app and the Trane Link thermostat leave a lot to be desired. They are both missing functionality that apps/thermostats like Nest and Eco Bee have had for a decade. 

1. No support for Matter or Apple Home Kit

2. No ability to gradually ramp up temperature to scheduled set points.

3. Kludges for things like detecting whether a home is occupied. 

4. Incomplete log data. The  controller, app, and thermostat know when the relay is closed for accessories like a humidifier, but this data is not logged in the event data on the Trane Home website.

5. No reports. While the Trane Home app seems to have access to a fairly rich dataset, no reports are available for runtime, efficiency, etc. (.I.e like Nest and Eco Bee). 

Finally, customer service seems lacking and dismissive. For the one or two feedback messages I’ve submitted through the Trane website, I’ve received dismissive replies with kludge work arounds offered and then the ticket is closed.   There is a lot of low hanging fruit here, but Trane doesn’t seem to have much interest in improving things. This could be a really slick app and platform, and even have access to an API for a subscription if Trane wanted to make some extra revenue. I guess it’s too much to expect an HVAC manufacturer to have an awesome dev team?

author: Rdt212
title: Worst home comfort app I’ve ever used
body:
When we spent $21,000 to have our furnace and A/C upgraded, part of the selling point was the exclusive Trane panel and mobile app. They sell you on how technologically advanced the system is and how much data it collects and analyzes. Super cool idea and selling point!

I have a hard time believing that when the panel itself can only do a fraction of what far cheaper/less exclusive panels can do. We had an OLD EcoBee before this, and it functioned in a far superior manner. The mobile app is absolute garbage, especially when compared to EcoBee or Nest. Half the time the data doesn’t even load. It deletes history, which tells me that if it can’t even show me the data, it’s definitely not using and learning from any data. The in-room monitors also cannot be viewed separately, which is frustrating if I’m curious how our 2nd floor bedroom is looking before we get home. All we can see is an “average of all monitors,” which is not helpful. And many times when I go to change a target temp setting in the mobile app, it thinks for a long while then times out and won’t process the change. I thought perhaps it was my phone, so then I used my spouse’s and a friend’s phone just to check and the same thing happened in their apps.

If you’re going to charge for a superior product, you’d better darn well have a superior product and product experience. Do better!

author: jatlygee
title: Great equipment, terrible cloud connectivity
body:
The service is very slow to respond and unreliable. Any time you have to change the temperature you have to stay on the screen until it finish loading, which is 5 - 10 seconds otherwise it doesn’t register the change. The app and the trane home service are in desperate need of an update.
We own a ux360 thermostat, which is completely locked down and has no ability to be connected directly to any local automation tools, which means if the Trane home service is unreliable so is your thermostat. So, if your wanting to have alternative for controlling the thermostat without Trane home service and app, you can’t . Please note that while the app offers integration with google home or Alexa, they both rely on Trane home service network, which is single point of failure. This should not be the case for a critical equipment such as an hvac system.

author: Mr. Gil Sir
title: Sketchy Performance
body:
After the first year of ownership, the thermostat worked perfectly. Then, over the next 12 months or more, it’s performance was sketchy at best. I called the installer to have it serviced, and of course when he checked it, it was operating within the norms and no issues were found. Although it’s covered under our purchase warranty, if they replaced it and the manufacturer found nothing wrong with the thermostat I would end up having to pay over $500 for its replacement; what a rip off.
Don’t get me wrong, the unit cools, and heats like it’s supposed to, and does a great job. It is the Trane thermostat that is the issue. 
I’m going to have it replaced at my own cost with a Honeywell product that cost about 130 bucks. i’m told they were the best; we’ll see.

author: LenCab
title: It works, but could be much better
body:
Overall, the app works, but it's just OK. On the positive side, the app appears to be stable and allows face ID so it doesn't sign me out constantly like some of my other smart-home-style apps. My main beef is that it doesn't display more system information on the dashboard, which would be nice given how quiet the newer HVAC systems. 

More details:

-The "Schedules" tab is really the only reason to use the app because it's much easier than the Trane Link UX360. 

-The display information on the home screen ("Dashboard") is not very useful and not customizable. It would be nice create custom views to display system information the user wants to see (like stage status and fan speed).

-The main menu brings up app-specific options, most of which are irrelevant for my use (geofences, videos, news).

-It's confusing to have "App Settings" in the menu and "Settings" on the bottom. The "App Settings" has some useful stuff like enabling face ID to sign in (very nice!) and "Settings" is more about your actual HVAC system (mode [off, auto, cool, heat], run mode [hold temp, run schedule], temperature scale, etc.). Some of the latter is useless like "filter size" and "send filter reminders." One problem is that the "Settings" page shows your HVAC Service Information, but you need to access "App Settings" to enable HVAC dealer access. That's a pretty poor design.

-The "Events" option is next to worthless. It does provide a history of things going on with the HVAC system, but it's not easy to read or find relevant information easily. I'd much rather have a display that shows system status (idle, cooling, heating, alert), stage status, and compressor speed.

author: SleeplessinStPete
title: App works perfectly fine, control panel I have a problem w
body:
When I wake up in the middle of the night I do not want to get on my phone to get on an app to change my temp. Worse is the control panel on the wall. U have to put glasses on, turn light on and play around with temp up/temp down/heat on/air conditioning on flat screen until you are awake.  Even if u leave the settings when u go to bed close to what u want they will switch from air conditioning to heat when u get up to try to change temp because the buttons r so small u can’t help but overlap the pad of your finger from one heat to air to temp up to temp down. I end up waking fully up. In 25 years of being in the same house we have replaced units, I believe, 3 times (different brand previous units). We like our current unit best but not the control panel. Previous units had an actual button that was the size of the pad of your finger. At night, w eyes closed, u could tap up or down for temp (never having to touch heat or air by accident). I know u can preset temp to automatically change in middle of night if that works for u. It doesn’t for us. 

This actual app works perfectly fine.

body: Our new home came with a Trane Comfortlink thermostat with Nexia built-in. I was very reluctant at first about moving from Ecobee (a device I consider to be more "open") to a platform locked in to our HVAC but the Nexia app has proven very useful and contains features (like Multi-user geofencing) that Ecobee and many others don't have. Only complaints are that sometimes Nexia occasionally thinks I'm away when I'm home then reverts back, or vice-versa which starts/stops the furnace. And when creating a thermostat automation with multiple zones, even though you select only some zones it activates all of them when it runs -- so you have to set the same action repeated for each zone in the automation.

The Nexia app works with Google Home, Amazon Alexa, and Google Assistant. See app menu settings "Enable Voice Assistant".

body: We just installed an American Standard HVAC system with the 824 thermostat.  Our "old" system had a wifi enabled thermostat with a mobile app.   We expected this mobile app to meet and exceed the functions of our former app.  The thermostat is out only device connected.   It delivered on our expectations with the responsive connection and quick relay of input to our system.  The ability to change the temp setting is fine.   We are very disappointed that we can't modify our schedule settings from the mobile app; we had this function with our previous thermostat.   As a single device (thermostat) user, this app has been disappointing.  It does not offer a full range of control of our thermostat.  The thermostat and system exceed our expectations.  The mobile app has been a disappointment in its restrictive functions.     We would love to recommend this app as highly as we recommend the system, but we cannot do this until there is an expansion of the function controls; primarily the ability to control and modify the schedule and fan speeds.   We'll remain optimistic that we'll enjoy increased satisfaction once these functions are included in the mobile app, but as it stands now, we DO grieve the loss of our previous app.       We'll look forward to your function expansion updates...soon, please?
